newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares surge higher, Endesa leads gains.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares surge higher, Endesa leads gains.

text.p: Chilean stocks rebounded to close sharply higher with the market driven by strong demand abroad for power giant Endesa, said traders.
The rally is seen resuming at the opening provided buy orders continue to flood in for the electricity generator, Chile's largest private company, they said.
"Last week's positive mood has continued. The market is being driven by arbitrage in Endesa," said one trader.
The 40-share IPSA index ended up 1.7 percent at 115.12 points. The general IGPA index climbed 1.08 percent at 5,353.72 points amid volume of 16.6 billion pesos.
Trade in Endesa accounted for one third of the total turnover, said dealers.
They reported heavy demand in New York for Endesa, which shot up 4.82 percent to close at 272 pesos.
Dealers were divided about the reasons for Endesa's rise with one reporting demand from a U.S. foreign investment fund, which is buying Latin American electricity stocks.
Another broker said Spanish power firm Endesa is having a second stab at buying a stake in the company, but this time is buying shares directly.
Last year the Spanish firm tried to buy a stake in the Enersis group, which controls Endesa, but the talks failed.
Endesa, which alone accounts for a 20 percent weighting in the IPSA index, has risen nearly 30 percent since the start of the year.
Other risers included steel-maker Cap, up 4.06 percent at 1,050 pesos, power utility Chilgener and bottler Andina, which gained 1.83 percent to 2,175 pesos.
Losers included forestry firm Masisa, down 1.32 percent to 225 pesos and telecom Entel which shed 0.18 percent to 2,845 pesos.
